category: MI admitted > 24 hrs after onset of ischemia
notes: ICD codes do not record time from symptom onset, so codes alone cannot separate this from 'Infarction, acute myocardial'. Assign here only if your data has symptom-onset and admission times showing > 24 h; otherwise these stays fall to the next row.

notes: Unstable angina (I20.0, I25.110, I25.7x0) is excluded; it's in the Cardiovascular group. I25.10 is optional: it captures 'asymptomatic' CAD but is a very common secondary code, so it will flag many patients.
Catches dissections not coded to a thoracic or abdominal site. Before FY2022, all aortic dissections coded to I71.0x without site detail.
Thoracoabdominal aneurysms (I71.5*, I71.6*) aren't an APACHE option; they're mapped to thoracic here. Move them to abdominal if you prefer.

category: Aortic aneurysm, site unspecified (not an APACHE option; counts toward the flag)
notes: Not one of your listed options, but these codes do indicate an aortic aneurysm.
Procedure category. Require an aneurysm diagnosis on the same stay: I71* for aortic procedures, I72* for 03V*/04V* (those roots also cover embolization and stenting for other reasons).
Require I25.3 AND one of the procedure codes on the same stay.

Ruptured cerebral aneurysms code as subarachnoid hemorrhage (I60.x) and belong in APACHE neuro categories, not here. Post-procedural pseudoaneurysms (e.g., femoral after cath) usually carry I72.x plus a complication code.

category: ARDS-adult respiratory distress syndrome, non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema
notes: J81.0 is meant for noncardiogenic edema; acute pulmonary edema due to heart disease codes to I50.x. Coders don't always follow that, so check J81.0 stays that also carry I50.x. Exclude J81.1 (chronic pulmonary edema).

Catch-all: placed after the angina, aneurysm and ARDS groups so it only gets circulatory codes no other category claims. For yes/no flags, likewise exclude codes matched by any other group. Use I99.8 / I77.8* if you want a narrower definition.
Your list includes this category twice ('ethanol' / 'bethanol'); treated as one category. Ethylene glycol codes to T52.3 (glycols), not T51.
Opioid analgesics (T40.x) are under Street drugs.

Medicinal lithium is indexed to T43.59 ('other antipsychotics'), which also covers atypical antipsychotics such as quetiapine and olanzapine. Codes alone can't separate them; T43.59 is kept under Sedatives/antipsychotics. To pull lithium out, use drug name or lithium level data.
T42.6 also includes some antiepileptics (e.g., valproate).

Prescription opioids (T40.2, T40.4) are included here because the APACHE wording says 'opiates'. T43.6 also includes caffeine (T43.61-); drop it if you want to be strict. Cannabis and hallucinogens are optional.

category: Toxicity, drug (i.e., beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, etc.)
notes: Includes adverse effects in therapeutic use (intent character 5), e.g., digoxin toxicity. The drug list is a starting point; add other classes as needed.

Placed after the agent-specific categories, so it catches intentional overdoses of agents not listed above. If you want intent to take precedence, move this category to the top of the toxicology group.
